title: Hypergraphs with the smallest Hall ratio are still hard to colour
summary: For $H$ a hypergraph, the Hall ratio $ρ(H)=\text{max}_{X\subseteq V(H)}\frac{\lvert{X}\rvert}{α(H[X])}$ is a natural lower bound for its chromatic number, and among non-empty $k$-uniform hypergraphs the smallest possible Hall ratio is $k/(k-1)$. For graphs ($k = 2$), having minimum Hall ratio $2$ forces chromatic number $2$. Nešetřil, Rödl, and Sales asked whether a similar phenomenon holds at higher uniformities. We answer this question negatively in a strong form, showing that for every $k \geqslant 3$ there are $k$-uniform hypergraphs with Hall ratio exactly $k/(k-1)$ and arbitrarily…
